finding.claim: DELETE /projects/:id calls authorized() which returns a boolean, but the result is discarded, so no authorization is enforced. Any authenticated user can delete any project. (Also, a missing project makes project.id/ownerId throw a TypeError on undefined, a minor 500.)
finding.source: Authenticated request with arbitrary :id in DELETE /projects/:id (req.params.id)

trace.note: route handler for DELETE /projects/:id; only req.user presence is assumed
project looked up by attacker-controlled id with no ownership filter
authorized(req.user, project) returns true/false (defined at api.js:12-14) but the return value is ignored; it does not throw

finding.guards_checked: authorize() (api.js:4) throws on failure, but this route calls authorized() instead, which only returns a boolean. No middleware is visible in this file; the router is mounted elsewhere, and no other ownership check exists on this path. Contrast with the PUT route at api.js:25, which correctly uses authorize().

verdict.guard_found: none effective: authorized() at api.js:12-14 returns a boolean that is discarded at api.js:18; authorize() (api.js:4-10, throws) is only used on the PUT route at api.js:25; no middleware visible in this file
verdict.reason: api.js:18 calls authorized() as a bare statement, discarding its boolean (defined at api.js:12-14), so api.js:19 deletes any project for any authenticated user, whereas the PUT route at api.js:25 correctly uses the throwing authorize().
